input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 14 gives Client a unilateral, no-cause right to terminate on written notice, with services (and therefore charges) running only to the last day of the month following the notice month — roughly 30–60 days' notice, within our preferred 30-day band and well inside the fallback. No early-termination fee or penalty attaches: fees are invoiced monthly in arrears under Section 5(a) (invoices paid within 15 days of receipt), so there is no prepaid-fee exposure and the absence of an express pro-rata refund mechanic is immaterial here (noted, not flagged). On the other side, TrueLink has no mid-term convenience right: Section 13's early-termination triggers are Client breach/default (for cause), and the only other exit is a mutual 30-day notice of intent not to renew at the end of each one-year term — an end-of-term non-renewal right the fallback contemplates, exercisable equally by us, in a 12-month (not multi-year) auto-renewing term. The 30- rather than 90-day non-renewal notice is a minor sub-element and symmetric in our favour, so we would not spend leverage on it. No redline proposed.
